source_note: Original practice questions aligned to the NCERT Curiosity Grade 6 chapter themes. These questions are not copied from the textbook and should be reviewed by a science teacher before production use.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is science mainly concerned with?
options: Studying the natural world using evidence
questions.answer: Studying the natural world using evidence
questions.why: Science uses observation, questions, investigations and evidence to understand the natural world.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which action is an observation?
options: Noticing that a leaf feels rough
Guessing why the leaf is rough
Deciding that all leaves are rough
Claiming the leaf will grow tomorrow
questions.answer: Noticing that a leaf feels rough
questions.why: An observation is something noticed directly with the senses or an instrument.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which tool helps measure the length of a table?
questions.why: A scale or measuring tape is used to measure length.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A possible explanation that can be tested is called a…
questions.why: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation that can be checked by investigation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should an investigation be based on evidence?
options: So that conclusions are supported by observations
So that results match a guess
So that measurements can be skipped
So that only one trial is needed
questions.answer: So that conclusions are supported by observations
questions.why: Evidence makes a scientific conclusion more reliable than an unsupported opinion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which item is useful for protecting eyes during a laboratory activity?
questions.why: Safety goggles protect the eyes from splashes and small particles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What should you do before using an unfamiliar laboratory material?
options: Read the instructions and ask the teacher
Mix it with every other material
questions.answer: Read the instructions and ask the teacher
questions.why: Following instructions and teacher guidance helps keep investigations safe.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which record is most useful for comparing observations over several days?
questions.why: A dated table organises observations so changes can be compared.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student tests whether sunlight affects plant growth. What should be changed between the two groups?
options: The plant type and soil together
The amount of water only in one group
questions.why: A fair test changes the factor being investigated and keeps other important conditions the same.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why are repeated trials useful in an investigation?
options: They help reveal whether a result is consistent
They remove the need to record data
They allow several variables to change at once
questions.answer: They help reveal whether a result is consistent
questions.why: Repeating a test can reveal variation and make results more reliable.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement is an inference rather than a direct observation?
options: The wet ground may have been caused by rain
questions.answer: The wet ground may have been caused by rain
questions.why: An inference is an explanation drawn from observations, not a direct observation itself.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student records the length of a seedling as 8 cm. This is a…
questions.why: A measurement expressed as a number is quantitative data.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is the fairest way to compare how quickly two paper towels absorb water?
options: Use equal-sized pieces and the same amount of water
Use different-sized pieces and different amounts
Change the water and towel at the same time
questions.answer: Use equal-sized pieces and the same amount of water
questions.why: Keeping the size and water amount the same makes the comparison fair.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is the best next step after collecting measurements?
options: Write a conclusion before reading the data
questions.why: Data should be organised and examined before a conclusion is drawn.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which sentence is a testable question?
options: Does the length of a shadow change during the day?
questions.answer: Does the length of a shadow change during the day?
questions.why: A testable question can be investigated through observations or measurements.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should a measuring instrument be read at eye level?
questions.why: Looking straight at a scale helps avoid parallax error.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Two groups of identical seedlings receive the same soil and water. One gets 2 hours of light and the other 6 hours. What is the independent variable?
questions.why: The independent variable is the factor deliberately changed: the duration of light.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A result differs greatly from the other readings. What is the most careful response?
options: Check the procedure and repeat the measurement
Change all other readings to match it
Report only the result that supports the guess
questions.answer: Check the procedure and repeat the measurement
questions.why: An unusual result should be checked and repeated rather than hidden or altered.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student wants to know whether a shadow's length changes with time. Which record would best answer the question?
options: Measure the shadow at regular time intervals
Draw a shadow without noting the time
Ask a friend to estimate it from memory
questions.answer: Measure the shadow at regular time intervals
questions.why: Regular measurements paired with times show how shadow length changes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A class finds that a paper spinner falls more slowly when its wings are wider. Which conclusion is best?
options: The results suggest wing width affected falling time in this test
Wider wings always make every object fall slowly
The result proves gravity has stopped
The spinner's mass was the only factor tested
questions.answer: The results suggest wing width affected falling time in this test
questions.why: A careful conclusion states what the evidence supports without claiming more than the test examined.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A place where an organism lives is its…
questions.why: A habitat is the natural home or surroundings of an organism.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is an example of an aquatic habitat?
questions.why: A pond is a water-based habitat.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which feature is found in all vertebrates?
questions.why: Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which animal is commonly adapted for swimming with gills?
questions.why: Fish use gills to take dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which one is a flowering plant?
questions.why: Hibiscus produces flowers; moss, ferns and pines do not produce flowers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A camel is well suited to life in a…
questions.why: Camels have features that help them live in hot, dry desert conditions.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What does biodiversity mean?
options: The variety of living organisms in an area or on Earth
The number of rocks in a place
questions.answer: The variety of living organisms in an area or on Earth
questions.why: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which group includes animals with feathers?
questions.why: Feathers are a defining feature of birds.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why do scientists classify organisms into groups?
options: To organise and study their similarities and differences
questions.answer: To organise and study their similarities and differences
questions.why: Classification helps organise the enormous variety of living things.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which pair belongs to the same broad group of mammals?
questions.why: Cows and whales are mammals; mammals breathe with lungs and feed their young with milk.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which feature best helps distinguish an insect from a spider?
options: An insect always lives in water
questions.why: Adult insects have six legs, while spiders have eight.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which plant group reproduces using spores rather than flowers and seeds?
questions.why: Ferns reproduce using spores and do not produce flowers or seeds.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A bird has a streamlined body and wings. These features are mainly related to…
questions.why: A streamlined body and wings help many birds fly efficiently.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement about amphibians is generally correct?
options: Many live part of their lives in water and part on land
They spend their whole lives in the open ocean
questions.answer: Many live part of their lives in water and part on land
questions.why: Amphibians such as frogs typically use aquatic and land habitats during their life cycle.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which feature helps a cactus reduce water loss?
questions.why: Spines have less surface area than broad leaves and help reduce water loss.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which organism-structure pair is correctly matched?
questions.why: Fish use gills for gas exchange in water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: An animal has eight legs and no backbone. Which group is the best match?
questions.why: Spiders and their relatives are arachnids; they have eight legs and no backbone.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Two plants grow in different habitats. One has broad leaves and the other has needle-like leaves. What is a reasonable scientific interpretation?
options: Their structures may be adaptations to different conditions
Both plants must be the same species
Leaf shape has no relationship to environment
questions.answer: Their structures may be adaptations to different conditions
questions.why: Plant structures often help organisms survive in their habitats.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which animal is a vertebrate that is also an amphibian?
questions.why: A frog has a backbone and belongs to the amphibian group.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A learner finds an unknown animal with six jointed legs, three body regions and antennae. Which group is the best classification?
questions.why: Six legs, three body regions and antennae are common identifying features of insects.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which nutrient is a major source of energy?
questions.why: Carbohydrates are an important energy source for the body.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which nutrient helps the body grow and repair tissues?
questions.why: Proteins are needed for growth and repair of body tissues.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which food is a good source of protein?
questions.why: Pulses provide plant protein.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which nutrient helps prevent constipation by supporting bowel movement?
questions.why: Dietary fibre adds bulk to food and supports healthy digestion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which vitamin is commonly linked with healthy eyesight?
questions.why: Vitamin A is important for normal vision.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Why is water important in our diet?
options: It helps transport substances and regulate body temperature
It provides all the body's energy
It makes bones out of air
questions.answer: It helps transport substances and regulate body temperature
questions.why: Water is needed for transport, temperature regulation and many body processes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: A diet containing suitable amounts of different nutrients is called…
questions.why: A balanced diet provides nutrients in appropriate amounts for health.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which is a good habit before eating?
options: Wash hands with soap and clean water
questions.answer: Wash hands with soap and clean water
questions.why: Handwashing helps prevent germs from entering the body through food.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which nutrient is especially important for building and repairing muscles?
questions.why: Proteins provide amino acids used to build and repair body tissues.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: A lack of vitamin C over a long period can cause…
questions.why: Vitamin C deficiency can cause scurvy, which affects gums and connective tissues.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which mineral is needed to make haemoglobin in blood?
questions.why: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which food combination is most likely to provide a mix of energy, protein and fibre?
questions.why: Rice supplies carbohydrates, dal supplies protein and vegetables add fibre and micronutrients.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Why should packaged-food labels be checked?
options: To learn about ingredients and nutrient amounts
To decide the colour of the packet
To avoid all fruits and vegetables
To make the food last forever
questions.answer: To learn about ingredients and nutrient amounts
questions.why: Labels can help people compare ingredients, serving sizes and nutrient information.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which deficiency is associated with night blindness?
questions.why: Vitamin A is essential for normal vision, especially in dim light.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which food is a useful source of calcium?
questions.why: Milk contains calcium, which helps build and maintain bones and teeth.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Why is eating a variety of foods generally better than eating only one food?
options: One food always contains every nutrient
Variety removes the need for water
questions.why: A varied diet is more likely to provide the range of nutrients the body needs.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: A child feels tired and a health worker finds low haemoglobin. Which dietary mineral may be lacking?
questions.why: Iron deficiency can lead to anaemia and tiredness because haemoglobin is reduced.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: Which meal is the most balanced choice?
options: Chapati, dal, vegetables, curd and fruit
questions.answer: Chapati, dal, vegetables, curd and fruit
questions.why: The meal combines cereals, protein foods, vegetables, dairy and fruit.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: A student drinks very little water on a hot day and plays outdoors. Which problem is more likely?
questions.why: Sweating causes water loss; not replacing it can lead to dehydration.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
questions.q: A person avoids all pulses, milk, eggs and other protein-rich foods without suitable alternatives. Which body function may be affected?
questions.why: Insufficient protein can affect growth and repair of body tissues.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which material is strongly attracted to an ordinary bar magnet?
questions.why: Iron is a magnetic material attracted by a magnet.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A bar magnet has how many poles?
questions.why: A bar magnet has a north pole and a south pole.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What happens when two north poles are brought close?
questions.why: Like magnetic poles repel each other.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What happens when a north pole and a south pole are brought close?
questions.why: Unlike magnetic poles attract each other.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which instrument uses a small magnet to show directions?
questions.why: A compass needle aligns approximately north–south.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which object is usually non-magnetic?
questions.why: Wood is not attracted by an ordinary magnet.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Where is the magnetic effect of a bar magnet usually strongest?
questions.why: The magnetic effect is strongest near the two poles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which pair contains two magnetic materials?
questions.why: Iron and nickel are magnetic materials.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest approximately along which direction?
questions.why: Earth's magnetic field makes a freely suspended magnet align roughly north–south.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which material can be used to make a simple compass needle?
questions.why: A magnetised steel needle can align with Earth's magnetic field.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What happens if a bar magnet is broken into two pieces?
options: Each piece has a north and a south pole
One piece becomes only north and the other only south
Only the broken surface becomes a pole
questions.answer: Each piece has a north and a south pole
questions.why: Breaking a magnet produces smaller magnets, each with two poles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which method can help separate iron filings from sand?
options: Move a magnet over the mixture
questions.answer: Move a magnet over the mixture
questions.why: The magnet attracts iron filings but not ordinary sand.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should a compass be kept away from a strong magnet while taking a direction reading?
options: The strong magnet can disturb the compass needle
The compass needle will become water
The magnet removes Earth's magnetic field
questions.answer: The strong magnet can disturb the compass needle
questions.why: Nearby magnets can deflect a compass needle and give a misleading direction.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which pole of a magnet is attracted to the south pole of another magnet?
questions.why: Unlike poles attract, so north is attracted to south.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A magnet attracts a paper clip but not a plastic button. What does this show?
options: Magnetic attraction depends on the material
The magnet attracts only round objects
questions.answer: Magnetic attraction depends on the material
questions.why: Iron or steel in the paper clip is attracted; plastic is not.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement about magnetic poles is correct?
options: A magnet always has both north and south poles
A magnet can have only a north pole
A magnet can have only a south pole
Poles exist only when the magnet is heated
questions.answer: A magnet always has both north and south poles
questions.why: Magnetic poles occur in pairs; isolated north or south poles are not obtained by breaking a bar magnet.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student wants to test whether a key is magnetic. Which procedure is best?
options: Bring a magnet near it and observe whether it is attracted
Check whether it floats in water
questions.answer: Bring a magnet near it and observe whether it is attracted
questions.why: A direct attraction test checks whether the key contains a magnetic material.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Two identical bar magnets are placed end to end with north facing north. What is expected?
options: They turn into one non-magnetic block
questions.why: North facing north means like poles are facing, so they repel.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A compass needle points north–south in one place but turns near a loudspeaker. What is a likely reason?
options: A magnet inside the loudspeaker affects the needle
Sound changes the compass into a thermometer
questions.answer: A magnet inside the loudspeaker affects the needle
questions.why: A loudspeaker contains a magnet that can deflect a nearby compass needle.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A mixture contains iron pins, salt and sand. Which sequence best separates the iron pins first?
options: Use a magnet before separating the salt and sand
Evaporate the mixture before adding water
Use a compass to dissolve the pins
Filter the dry mixture through cloth
questions.answer: Use a magnet before separating the salt and sand
questions.why: A magnet can remove the iron pins first; water-based methods can then separate salt and sand.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is the SI unit of length?
questions.why: The SI base unit of length is the metre.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: How many centimetres are in one metre?
questions.why: One metre is equal to 100 centimetres.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which instrument is suitable for measuring the length of a pencil?
questions.why: A ruler is suitable for measuring a small straight length.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: An object is in motion when its position changes with respect to…
questions.why: Motion is a change in position relative to a reference point over time.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is an example of circular motion?
options: The hands of a clock moving around its dial
A book resting on a desk
A stone lying on the ground
questions.answer: The hands of a clock moving around its dial
questions.why: Clock hands move along circular paths around the centre.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which unit is most suitable for the distance between two towns?
questions.why: Distances between towns are conveniently expressed in kilometres.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What should your eye do when reading a ruler?
options: Look from a very slanting angle
Look at the ruler from behind the table
questions.why: Viewing from directly above the mark helps avoid parallax error.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A swing moving to and fro repeats its motion. This is an example of…
questions.why: Periodic motion repeats at regular intervals.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: How many millimetres are in one centimetre?
questions.why: One centimetre equals ten millimetres.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A curved line is difficult to measure with a straight ruler. Which method is useful?
options: Place a thread along the curve, then measure the thread
questions.answer: Place a thread along the curve, then measure the thread
questions.why: A flexible thread can follow a curve and then be straightened for measurement.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A car moves along a straight road. Which type of motion is this?
questions.why: Motion along a straight line is rectilinear motion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A wheel rotating about its axle shows…
options: No change in position of any point
questions.why: The wheel turns about an axis, which is rotational motion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should a ruler's zero mark be placed at one end of the object?
options: So the measured length is the difference from the starting point
So the unit becomes a kilogram
questions.answer: So the measured length is the difference from the starting point
questions.why: Starting at zero makes the reading at the other end equal to the length.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A runner completes one lap of a circular track. Which path did the runner follow?
questions.why: A lap around a circular track follows a circular path.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student measures a strip as 4 cm and 6 mm. What is its length in millimetres?
questions.why: 4 cm = 40 mm; 40 mm + 6 mm = 46 mm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is the best way to measure the length of a curved leaf edge?
options: Use a thread along the edge and then a ruler
Stretch the leaf until it is straight
Measure its area with a clock
Use a compass needle as a scale
questions.answer: Use a thread along the edge and then a ruler
questions.why: A thread can follow the curved edge without forcing the leaf into a new shape.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student reads 5.2 cm when the line starts at 1.0 cm on the ruler. What is the line's length?
questions.why: Length = final reading − starting reading = 5.2 − 1.0 = 4.2 cm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which example best shows that motion depends on the reference point?
options: A seated passenger is at rest relative to the bus but moving relative to the road
A parked bus changes its colour
A ruler becomes shorter at night
questions.answer: A seated passenger is at rest relative to the bus but moving relative to the road
questions.why: The passenger's motion description changes with the chosen reference point.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A child walks 3 m forward and then 2 m back along the same straight path. What total distance has the child travelled?
questions.why: Total distance is the path length: 3 m + 2 m = 5 m.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A measurement is repeatedly larger when the ruler is viewed from the left and smaller from the right. What should be corrected?
options: The eye position while reading the scale
questions.answer: The eye position while reading the scale
questions.why: Slant viewing produces parallax error; the eye should be directly above the reading.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which word describes a material that lets most light pass through clearly?
questions.why: Transparent materials allow light to pass through so objects can be seen clearly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which material is usually opaque?
options: Pure water in a thin layer
questions.why: Wood does not allow light to pass through.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A substance that dissolves in water is called…
questions.why: A soluble substance forms a solution when it dissolves in a solvent.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which substance is commonly soluble in water?
questions.why: Salt dissolves in water to form a solution.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which material is generally flexible?
questions.why: Rubber can bend or stretch and return towards its original shape.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which object is most likely to float in water?
questions.why: Cork is less dense than water and generally floats.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which property describes how easily a material can be scratched?
questions.why: Hardness describes resistance to scratching or indentation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which item is made from a metal?
questions.why: Aluminium is a metal.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why do we group materials by their properties?
options: To choose suitable materials for different uses
To make all materials behave alike
To change their chemical identity by naming them
questions.answer: To choose suitable materials for different uses
questions.why: Knowing properties helps select materials for particular purposes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which material-property pair is correctly matched?
questions.why: Clear glass allows light through and objects can be seen clearly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which material is insoluble in water?
questions.why: Sand does not dissolve in water and can settle or be filtered out.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A material is translucent when it…
options: Allows some light through but does not show clear images
Allows clear viewing like clean glass
questions.answer: Allows some light through but does not show clear images
questions.why: Translucent materials transmit light but scatter it, so images are not clear.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which property is most important when choosing cloth for a raincoat?
questions.why: A raincoat should resist water passing through it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why can a metal pan be useful for cooking?
questions.why: Metal pans transfer heat from the stove to the food efficiently.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Two objects have the same size but different masses. Which statement is reasonable?
options: They may be made of materials with different densities
They must have the same material
questions.answer: They may be made of materials with different densities
questions.why: Density depends on mass for a given volume, so equal volumes can have different masses.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which material is best for a window if clear viewing is needed?
questions.why: A window needs a transparent material to allow light and a clear view.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student mixes sand and salt with water. Which observation is expected?
options: Salt dissolves but sand remains undissolved
Sand dissolves while salt floats as a gas
questions.answer: Salt dissolves but sand remains undissolved
questions.why: Salt is soluble in water; sand is insoluble.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why is stainless steel commonly used for spoons?
options: It is strong, durable and does not rust easily
questions.answer: It is strong, durable and does not rust easily
questions.why: Stainless steel is durable and resists corrosion in ordinary use.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A material lets light through but makes a person behind it look blurred. How should it be classified?
questions.why: A translucent material transmits scattered light, so details appear blurred.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A school needs a light, strong material for a reusable water bottle. Which choice is most sensible among these?
questions.why: A suitable bottle material must be durable, light and safe for contact with drinking water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?
questions.why: A thermometer is designed to measure temperature.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which unit is commonly used in school thermometers in India?
questions.why: Temperature is commonly recorded in degrees Celsius (°C).

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which thermometer is designed to measure human body temperature?
questions.why: A clinical thermometer is designed for body temperature measurements.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: At standard atmospheric pressure, water freezes at about…
questions.why: Pure water freezes at approximately 0 °C at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at about…
questions.why: Pure water boils at approximately 100 °C at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should a thermometer be read at eye level?
questions.why: Eye-level reading reduces parallax error.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which thermometer is suitable for measuring hot water in a laboratory?
questions.why: A laboratory thermometer has a wider temperature range for experiments.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What should you avoid doing with a glass thermometer?
questions.why: A glass thermometer can break and release its contents, so it must be handled carefully.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why is a clinical thermometer's range narrower than a laboratory thermometer's range?
options: It is designed for the limited range of human body temperatures
It is designed to measure boiling metals
It does not contain a scale
questions.answer: It is designed for the limited range of human body temperatures
questions.why: Clinical thermometers are made for body temperatures rather than a wide range of experiments.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A thermometer reads 28 °C. What does this number describe?
options: The temperature of the measured object or surroundings
questions.answer: The temperature of the measured object or surroundings
questions.why: A temperature reading describes how hot or cold the measured system is.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is the approximate normal body temperature often used as a reference?
questions.why: About 37 °C is a commonly used reference value; normal body temperature varies between people and times.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should a laboratory thermometer generally be kept upright while taking a reading?
options: To keep the scale and liquid column easy to read correctly
To increase the mass of the bulb
questions.answer: To keep the scale and liquid column easy to read correctly
questions.why: Keeping the thermometer upright and the bulb properly placed supports a reliable reading.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is the safest way to measure the temperature of hot water?
options: Use a suitable laboratory thermometer under teacher guidance
Touch the water with a finger
Use a clinical thermometer beyond its range
questions.answer: Use a suitable laboratory thermometer under teacher guidance
questions.why: A suitable laboratory thermometer measures hot water without direct contact.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A person has a body temperature of 39 °C. Compared with the 37 °C reference value, it is…

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should the bulb of a liquid-in-glass thermometer be surrounded by the substance being measured?
options: So it can reach the substance's temperature
So the liquid changes colour permanently
questions.answer: So it can reach the substance's temperature
questions.why: The bulb senses temperature and should be in good thermal contact with the measured substance.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement is correct about temperature and touch?
options: Touch gives only a rough sense and may be misleading
Touch always gives an exact Celsius value
questions.answer: Touch gives only a rough sense and may be misleading
questions.why: Our sense of hot and cold is relative and cannot provide an accurate numerical reading.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student measures hot water with a clinical thermometer that only covers body temperatures. What is the main problem?
options: The water may be outside the thermometer's range
The thermometer will measure the water's length
The water will become colder immediately
The thermometer will show the water's colour
questions.answer: The water may be outside the thermometer's range
questions.why: A clinical thermometer is not designed for the broad temperatures used in laboratory experiments.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A thermometer is moved from a cool room into warm water. Why should the student wait before noting the reading?
options: The thermometer needs time to reach the water's temperature
The numbers on the scale need to change order
questions.answer: The thermometer needs time to reach the water's temperature
questions.why: The reading stabilises after the thermometer and water reach thermal equilibrium.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A lab thermometer reading is taken while the bulb touches the bottom of a heated beaker. Why may this be inaccurate?
options: The bottom may be hotter than the water being measured
The Celsius scale turns into a length scale
questions.answer: The bottom may be hotter than the water being measured
questions.why: Contact with the heated vessel can make the bulb read the vessel's temperature rather than the water's bulk temperature.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student records 31 °C, 30 °C and 31 °C in repeated measurements. What is the best report?
options: Report the readings and note that they are close together
Keep only the highest value without explanation
questions.answer: Report the readings and note that they are close together
questions.why: Reporting repeated readings transparently shows the small variation in measurements.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: What is the solid state of water called?
questions.why: Ice is water in its solid state.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: What is the gaseous state of water called?
questions.why: Water vapour is water in the gaseous state.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: The change from ice to liquid water is called…
questions.why: Melting changes a solid into a liquid.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: The change from liquid water to ice is called…
questions.why: Freezing changes a liquid into a solid.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: The change of liquid water into water vapour from its surface is…
questions.why: Evaporation is the change from liquid to gas at the surface.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Water droplets forming on the outside of a cold glass are caused by…
options: Condensation of water vapour in the air
questions.answer: Condensation of water vapour in the air
questions.why: Water vapour in air cools and condenses into liquid droplets on the cold surface.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Which process forms clouds from water vapour?
questions.why: Water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets or ice crystals that form clouds.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Which process returns water from clouds to Earth's surface?
questions.why: Rain, snow and hail are forms of precipitation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Which condition generally increases the rate of evaporation?
options: A colder surrounding with no airflow
questions.why: More exposed liquid surface allows more particles to escape into the air.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Why do wet clothes dry faster on a warm, windy day?
options: Warmth and moving air increase evaporation
questions.answer: Warmth and moving air increase evaporation
questions.why: Higher temperature and moving air help water evaporate faster.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Which is an example of evaporation causing cooling?
questions.why: Evaporation takes energy from the skin and produces a cooling effect.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: What drives the water cycle on Earth mainly?
options: Energy from the Sun and gravity
questions.answer: Energy from the Sun and gravity
questions.why: Solar energy drives evaporation, while gravity helps water fall and flow back.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Which sequence best represents part of the water cycle?
questions.why: Water evaporates, cools and condenses into clouds, then returns as precipitation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Why does water evaporate from a puddle even when it is not boiling?
options: Some surface particles have enough energy to escape
The ground pulls every water molecule into the air
questions.answer: Some surface particles have enough energy to escape
questions.why: Evaporation can occur at temperatures below the boiling point because energetic surface molecules escape.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Which change is reversible by cooling water vapour?
questions.why: Cooling water vapour can condense it back to liquid water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Why does a wet floor dry faster when air can move over it?
options: Moving air carries away water vapour near the surface
Moving air changes water into salt
The floor becomes hotter than the Sun
questions.answer: Moving air carries away water vapour near the surface
questions.why: Air movement removes humid air near the floor, allowing more evaporation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: A cold bottle taken from a refrigerator becomes wet on its outside. Where did the water come from?
options: Water vapour present in the surrounding air
Water passing through the bottle wall
The liquid inside turning into ice outside
questions.answer: Water vapour present in the surrounding air
questions.why: Moisture in the surrounding air condenses on the chilled bottle surface.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: A shallow plate and a narrow glass contain equal amounts of water in the same room. Which is likely to evaporate faster?
options: The water in the shallow plate
The water in the narrow glass
Both must evaporate at exactly the same rate
questions.answer: The water in the shallow plate
questions.why: The shallow plate exposes a larger surface area to the air.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes boiling from evaporation?
options: Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at its boiling point; evaporation occurs at the surface
Boiling occurs only at the surface
They are exactly the same process in every condition
questions.answer: Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at its boiling point; evaporation occurs at the surface
questions.why: Boiling forms vapour throughout the liquid at a specific pressure-dependent temperature, while evaporation occurs at the surface over a range of temperatures.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: A Journey through States of Water
questions.q: A student wants to reduce water loss from a stored open container. Which action is most effective?
options: Cover the container with a suitable lid
Blow warm air across the surface
questions.answer: Cover the container with a suitable lid
questions.why: A lid reduces the exposed surface and limits water vapour escaping into the surroundings.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method removes visible stones from rice by hand?
questions.why: Handpicking removes large, visible unwanted particles manually.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method uses wind to separate lighter husk from heavier grains?
questions.why: Winnowing uses moving air to carry away lighter husk while heavier grains fall.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method separates bran from flour using a mesh?
questions.why: A sieve allows smaller particles to pass through while larger ones remain.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method can separate tea leaves from tea?
questions.why: A strainer acts as a filter and holds back tea leaves.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method can obtain salt from salt water?
questions.why: Water evaporates and salt remains behind.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which process allows heavier insoluble particles to settle at the bottom?
questions.why: During sedimentation, denser insoluble particles settle under gravity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Pouring clear liquid off after sediment settles is called…
questions.why: Decantation carefully pours the liquid away from settled solids.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method separates iron filings from sand?
options: Sieving with a very fine cloth only
questions.why: A magnet attracts iron filings and leaves the sand behind.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method separates grains from stalks after harvesting?
questions.why: Threshing separates grain seeds from stalks or husks.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: A mixture contains sand and water. Which method is suitable for quickly removing the sand?
questions.why: A filter retains insoluble sand while water passes through.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which method is used to separate butter from curd by churning?
questions.why: Churning helps separate butter or cream from curd or buttermilk.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Why is sedimentation often followed by decantation?
options: The solid settles first, then the clearer liquid is poured off
The mixture changes into a gas
questions.answer: The solid settles first, then the clearer liquid is poured off
questions.why: Sedimentation settles the solid; decantation separates the clearer liquid above it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which mixture can be separated by winnowing?
questions.why: The lighter husk is blown away while heavier grains fall.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: A cook wants to remove small stones from lentils. Which method is most suitable?
questions.why: Stones that are visible and few in number can be removed by handpicking.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Which sequence is suitable for separating muddy water when the mud is allowed to settle first?
questions.why: Mud settles at the bottom; the clearer water can then be poured off.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: Why can ordinary filtration not remove salt that has dissolved completely in water?
options: Dissolved salt particles pass through the filter with the water
Salt is attracted by every filter
The filter turns salt into gas
questions.answer: Dissolved salt particles pass through the filter with the water
questions.why: Dissolved particles are much smaller than the filter pores and remain in the filtrate.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: A mixture contains iron pins, sand and salt. Which should be done first?
options: Remove the iron pins with a magnet
Evaporate all the salt before removing iron
Use a sieve to remove dissolved salt
Add oil and churn the mixture
questions.answer: Remove the iron pins with a magnet
questions.why: Magnetic separation removes the iron without mixing it with the other components.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: After removing iron pins from sand and salt, what is a suitable next step to separate salt from sand?
options: Add water to dissolve salt, then filter the sand
Use a compass to attract salt
Winnow the mixture in still air
questions.answer: Add water to dissolve salt, then filter the sand
questions.why: Salt dissolves in water while sand does not; filtration retains the sand.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: After filtering a salt solution, how can solid salt be obtained?
options: Use handpicking on the clear liquid
questions.why: Evaporation removes water and leaves the dissolved salt behind.

questions.subject: Science
questions.concept: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
questions.q: A mixture contains two solids of similar size but one is magnetic. Which method is most selective?
questions.why: A magnet separates based on magnetic property rather than particle size.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is a basic characteristic of living organisms?
options: They are always able to fly
They are always larger than stones
questions.why: Living organisms carry out processes such as nutrition, respiration, growth and reproduction.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which process releases energy from food in living cells?
questions.why: Respiration releases usable energy from food within living organisms.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which process removes waste products from the body?
questions.why: Excretion removes metabolic waste from an organism.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A plant bends towards light. This is an example of…
questions.why: Light is a stimulus, and the plant responds by growing towards it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which organism reproduces by laying eggs?
questions.why: A hen is an animal that reproduces by laying eggs.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which object is non-living?
questions.why: A stone does not perform life processes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is the basic structural unit of living organisms?
questions.why: Cells are the basic structural and functional units of living organisms.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement about plant movement is correct?
options: Plants show movements, even though they do not walk from place to place
Plants never respond to their surroundings
questions.answer: Plants show movements, even though they do not walk from place to place
questions.why: Plants show growth-related and other movements, such as shoots bending towards light.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why is a seed considered living even when it appears inactive?
options: It can germinate and resume growth under suitable conditions
It cannot carry out any life process
questions.answer: It can germinate and resume growth under suitable conditions
questions.why: A viable seed may remain dormant and germinate when conditions become suitable.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which of these is an example of growth in a living organism?
options: A young plant increasing in height
questions.answer: A young plant increasing in height
questions.why: Growth is a lasting increase in size or development of an organism.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which life process helps organisms obtain materials needed for energy and growth?
questions.why: Nutrition is the process of obtaining or making food needed by organisms.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which response is shown when a person pulls a hand away from a hot object?
questions.why: Heat causes a stimulus and the nervous system triggers a quick response.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why is a flame not classified as a living organism even though it can grow and use fuel?
options: It does not have cells and does not carry out all life processes
It moves from place to place
questions.answer: It does not have cells and does not carry out all life processes
questions.why: A flame is a chemical process, not a cellular organism; it does not reproduce biologically or have cells.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which observation is the strongest evidence that a seed is viable?
options: It germinates and produces a seedling under suitable conditions
It is kept in a closed box forever
It is heavier than a grain of sand
questions.answer: It germinates and produces a seedling under suitable conditions
questions.why: Germination demonstrates that the seed is alive and capable of growth.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which pair correctly matches a life process with its function?
questions.why: Excretion removes waste products formed during life activities.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A plant's roots grow downwards while its shoot grows upwards. What does this show?
options: Different plant parts respond to gravity in different ways
Plants have no response to stimuli
questions.answer: Different plant parts respond to gravity in different ways
questions.why: Roots and shoots show directional growth responses to gravity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A dormant seed does not visibly grow for weeks. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: It may still be alive and waiting for suitable conditions
questions.answer: It may still be alive and waiting for suitable conditions
questions.why: Dormancy is a resting state; a viable seed can remain alive without visible growth.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes a living thing from a moving toy car?
options: A living thing carries out cellular life processes
A toy car can move, so it must be alive
A living thing must always change colour
A toy car is alive when its battery works
questions.answer: A living thing carries out cellular life processes
questions.why: Movement alone does not prove life; living organisms perform a range of cellular life processes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: An organism takes in food, releases energy, removes wastes and produces offspring. What does this combination indicate?
options: It is carrying out several life processes
It is a type of mineral
questions.answer: It is carrying out several life processes
questions.why: Nutrition, respiration, excretion and reproduction are characteristic life processes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student says that a plant is non-living because it cannot walk. Which response is scientifically sound?
options: Plants are living because they grow, respire, reproduce and respond to stimuli
Walking is the only test of life
Plants are living only when they have flowers
questions.answer: Plants are living because they grow, respire, reproduce and respond to stimuli
questions.why: Walking is not required for life; plants carry out essential life processes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is a natural resource?
questions.why: Water occurs in nature and is an important natural resource.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which gas do humans need for respiration?
questions.why: Humans use oxygen during cellular respiration.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which resource is renewable on a human timescale?
questions.why: Sunlight is continually supplied by the Sun and is renewable.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which resource is a fossil fuel?
questions.why: Coal formed from ancient plant remains over geological time.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why are forests important?
options: They provide habitats and help maintain ecological balance
questions.answer: They provide habitats and help maintain ecological balance
questions.why: Forests support biodiversity, soil protection, water cycling and many livelihoods.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which action helps conserve water at home?
options: Washing one item under a running hose for a long time
questions.why: Repairing leaks prevents unnecessary water loss.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is soil erosion?
options: Removal of the topsoil by wind or water
questions.answer: Removal of the topsoil by wind or water
questions.why: Soil erosion occurs when topsoil is carried away by wind or water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which practice helps reduce waste?
options: Reuse a container when it is safe and suitable
Throw every item away after one use
questions.answer: Reuse a container when it is safe and suitable
questions.why: Reusing suitable items reduces the amount of waste generated.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why should fossil fuels be used carefully?
options: They take millions of years to form and are finite
They are made from sunlight stored overnight
questions.answer: They take millions of years to form and are finite
questions.why: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are non-renewable on human timescales.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which energy source uses moving air?
questions.why: Wind turbines convert the energy of moving air into electrical energy.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which layer of soil is usually richest in humus?
questions.why: Topsoil commonly contains humus and many organisms that support plant growth.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which action can reduce soil erosion on a slope?
options: Growing vegetation with roots that hold soil
Running water over the slope continuously
questions.answer: Growing vegetation with roots that hold soil
questions.why: Plant roots help bind soil and reduce erosion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which resource is non-renewable?
questions.why: Petroleum is a fossil fuel that takes very long periods to form.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What does the 3R approach stand for?
questions.why: The 3R approach encourages reducing consumption, reusing items and recycling materials.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why is biodiversity valuable to an ecosystem?
options: Different organisms support interconnected ecological roles
It removes the need for habitats
questions.answer: Different organisms support interconnected ecological roles
questions.why: Different species contribute to food webs, pollination, decomposition and ecosystem stability.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which is a responsible use of groundwater?
options: Use water efficiently and allow recharge through rainwater harvesting
Waste it because it is underground
Cover every recharge area with concrete
questions.answer: Use water efficiently and allow recharge through rainwater harvesting
questions.why: Efficient use and recharge help protect groundwater supplies.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A village removes most trees from a hillside. Which effect is more likely during heavy rain?
questions.why: Without plant cover and roots, rain can carry more topsoil downhill.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which pair contains only renewable energy sources?
questions.why: Wind and sunlight are replenished naturally on human timescales.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why is rainwater harvesting useful in places with seasonal rainfall?
options: It stores or directs rainwater for later use and groundwater recharge
It turns rain into fossil fuel
questions.answer: It stores or directs rainwater for later use and groundwater recharge
questions.why: Rainwater harvesting can capture seasonal rain for later use or recharge.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A school wants to reduce its environmental impact. Which plan is best?
options: Save water and electricity, segregate waste and plant native trees
Burn mixed waste in the playground
Leave lights on in empty rooms
Use disposable items for every activity
questions.answer: Save water and electricity, segregate waste and plant native trees
questions.why: A combined plan conserves resources, manages waste and supports local biodiversity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is the Sun?
questions.why: The Sun is a star that produces its own light and heat.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.why: Earth is the planet on which humans live.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is the Moon in relation to Earth?
questions.why: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What causes day and night on Earth?
options: Earth's revolution around the Sun only
questions.why: Earth rotates, bringing different regions into and out of sunlight.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: How long does Earth take approximately to revolve once around the Sun?
questions.why: Earth takes about 365¼ days to complete one revolution around the Sun.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which object gives Earth most of its natural light during the day?
questions.why: Sunlight illuminates Earth during daytime.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A group of stars forming a recognisable pattern is called a…
questions.why: A constellation is a named pattern or region of stars in the sky.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which object is a planet?
questions.why: Jupiter is a planet orbiting the Sun.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why does the Moon appear bright in the night sky?
options: It produces sunlight like a star
It is made of glowing gas
questions.why: The Moon does not make its own visible light; it reflects sunlight.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which sequence lists the first four planets outward from the Sun?
questions.why: The first four planets from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What is an artificial satellite?
options: A human-made object placed in orbit around Earth or another body
questions.answer: A human-made object placed in orbit around Earth or another body
questions.why: Artificial satellites are launched by people for communication, weather, navigation and research.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which object is mostly made of ice, dust and rock and may form a tail near the Sun?
questions.why: Comets contain ice and dust; heating near the Sun can release gas and dust that form a tail.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: What causes the phases of the Moon?
options: We see different portions of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth
Earth's shadow covers it every night
The Moon changes its actual shape
The Sun switches off part of the Moon
questions.answer: We see different portions of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth
questions.why: The Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun changes the visible illuminated portion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which movement of Earth is mainly responsible for the yearly cycle?
options: The Sun orbiting Earth every day
questions.why: Earth's revolution around the Sun defines a year.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why do stars usually look like tiny points of light?
options: They are smaller than grains of sand
Earth's atmosphere turns them into planets
questions.why: Stars are enormous but appear tiny because of their great distances.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement about the solar system is correct?
options: The Sun is at its centre and planets orbit it
Earth is at the centre and the Sun orbits Earth
The Moon is the largest star
questions.answer: The Sun is at its centre and planets orbit it
questions.why: The solar system consists of the Sun and objects gravitationally bound to it, including planets.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Why do we see different phases of the Moon over a month?
options: The Moon changes position in its orbit around Earth
Clouds permanently cover parts of the Moon
Earth's rotation changes the Moon's surface
questions.answer: The Moon changes position in its orbit around Earth
questions.why: The orbit changes the angle from which we see the Moon's illuminated half.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which statement best explains seasons on Earth?
options: Earth's tilted axis and revolution around the Sun change sunlight angle and day length
Earth becomes much closer to the Sun every summer
The Moon blocks sunlight for half the year
questions.answer: Earth's tilted axis and revolution around the Sun change sunlight angle and day length
questions.why: Earth's axial tilt combined with its revolution causes seasonal differences in sunlight and day length.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which object is a small rocky body that orbits the Sun, mostly found in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter?
questions.why: Asteroids are rocky or metallic small bodies orbiting the Sun; many are in the main asteroid belt.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: A student sees the Moon as a thin crescent. Which statement is correct?
options: Only a small part of the Moon's sunlit half is visible from Earth
The Moon has physically lost most of its material
The Moon has stopped reflecting sunlight
Earth's shadow always makes the crescent
questions.answer: Only a small part of the Moon's sunlit half is visible from Earth
questions.why: A crescent phase occurs when only a small portion of the illuminated half is visible from Earth.
